document_check.note: The document is Ding et al. (2023), 'Prediction of progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease with longitudinal and multimodal data', Frontiers in Dementia 2:1271680. It compares an ADNI LSTM on five timepoints with random forests at a single index visit, as the review describes.

cited_result: Discrimination for 2-year MCI-to-AD progression (347 participants, 77 converters). The LSTM on five timepoints had AUC 0.93 ± 0.06; the random forest at the single 24-month index visit had AUC 0.90 ± 0.09 (DeLong P = 0.039). A random forest given all five timepoints had AUC 0.89 ± 0.10 (0.87 using the timepoint means).
tool_reason: The cited result is the discrimination (AUC) of competing multivariable machine-learning prognostic models for MCI-to-AD conversion.

domains.rationale: ADNI is an appropriate prospective cohort, but exclusions depend on outcome and follow-up. Participants who reverted to normal (n = 19) were excluded, as were 187 of 553 (34%) whose status at 48 months could not be determined. The sample was also restricted to those with complete NP and MRI data at all five visits.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used (cohort, RCT or nested case-control data)?
signalling.quote: This study included participants from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), a large-scale multi-center longitudinal study.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: The participants who either reverted to normal cognitive status (n = 19) or cannot determine the cognitive status at the 48-month follow-up examination (n = 187) were excluded.

domains.rationale: NP tests and FreeSurfer MRI volumes follow standard ADNI protocols, are collected before the outcome window, and would be available at the index exam, provided the five prior visits exist.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: In summary, the study utilized T1-weighted images acquired from ADNI-approved 3 T scanners, which were cross-sectionally processed using the 2010 Desikan-Killiany atlas with FreeSurfer image analysis suite, version 5.1.

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: was developed to predict the risk of progression from MCI to AD within 2 years from the index exam (the exam at 24-month).

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: First, our proposed method relies on longitudinal data and thus requires each subject to have the corresponding modality data across multiple time points.

domains.rationale: Conversion is an ADNI clinical diagnosis made with MMSE, CDR and logical memory. The same instruments (MMSE, CDR-SB, LDELTOTAL, FAQ and others) are predictors, so the predictors are part of the outcome definition and the outcome is determined with knowledge of them. The authors call this circular. Missing diagnoses were interpolated.

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: we interpolated the diagnosis by the status from the immediate prior and follow up exams if the diagnosis was consistent

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: The study utilized several measures including subjective memory concern, the Logical Memory Test (LMT), Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE), Clinical Dementia Rating scale (CDR), and the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke and the Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Disorders Association Alzheimer’s Criteria (NINCDS-ADRDA) to diagnose MCI and AD.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: Using NP tests for the diagnosis of AD and MCI can be circular, as these conditions are diagnosed based on the severity of cognitive dysfunction.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: More details on ADNI’s diagnostic criteria and methods can be found in General Procedures Manual on the ADNI website

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: In this study, we included 15 NP tests such as the functional assessment questionnaire (FAQ)

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Participants were followed up for 2 years since the index exam (equivalent to 48-months since the baseline exam), during which 77 (22.2%) were converted to AD.

domains.rationale: There are 77 events for about 24 candidate predictors per visit (15 NP tests, 6 to 7 MRI measures, 3 demographics): about 3 events per predictor for the single-visit random forest, and far fewer per input for the roughly 108 LSTM inputs. Participants with unknown outcome were excluded. Only AUC is reported, with no calibration. The paper does not describe nesting between hyperparameter tuning and performance estimation. Normalisation and MICE imputation are not stated to have been done inside the folds. The LSTM was tuned by Bayesian optimisation, while the random-forest comparator used 100 trees with no tuning described. There is no external validation.

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: The study included 347 participants with MCI at 24-month (age: mean 75, SD 7 years; 39.8% women) from ADNI, of whom 77 converted to AD

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: All continuous variables (i.e., NP test scores and MRI measures) were normalized to have a mean of zero and standard deviation of one.

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: cannot determine the cognitive status at the 48-month follow-up examination (n = 187) were excluded

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: In the analysis, variables with missing values comprising more than 50% were excluded. Multiple imputations using the chained equations (MICE) method (Azur et al., 2011) was used to impute the remaining features with missing values.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: The MRI measures included in this study were hippocampus volume, entorhinal cortex volume, middle temporal gyrus volume, fusiform volume, ventricle volume, whole brain volume, and intracranial volume.

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data (e.g. repeated measures) accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: LSTM is a type of recurrent neural network that is well-suited to modeling sequential data

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately, including calibration?
signalling.quote: The objective function being optimized was the average area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) across all folds.

signalling.question: 4.8 Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism in model performance accounted for?
signalling.quote: The optimization was performed using two separate 10-fold cross-validation procedures for hyperparameter selection and model performance evaluation.

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for a specification of the final LSTM and random-forest models (weights, variable importance, final architecture). The only statement found is 'We further built the model based on the selected best hyperparameters and evaluate its 2-year risk prediction performance.' (page 4).

signalling.question: AI: Is the train/test split at the participant level (no data from one person on both sides)?
signalling.quote: A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model using data collected at ﬁve-time points (baseline, 6, 12, 18, and 24-month) was developed

signalling.question: AI: Are preprocessing, imputation, feature selection and hyperparameter tuning done within training folds only?
signalling.quote: Searched the Methods and Statistical analyses for any statement that normalisation, MICE imputation or Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation were confined to training folds. None was found; normalisation and imputation are described as applied to the variables in general.

signalling.question: AI: Is the test set held out from all tuning?
signalling.quote: We implemented Bayesian optimization (Snoek et al., 2012) to search for the best hyperparameters for the LSTM model.

signalling.question: AI: Was class imbalance considered and handled?
signalling.quote: Searched for class weighting, resampling or any handling of the 22.2% event rate (77 converters vs 270 non-converters). None was described.

signalling.question: AI: Is reported performance apparent, internally validated or externally validated?
signalling.quote: Future studies with larger sample sizes should be considered to validate the results.

overall: High risk of bias (PROBAST: domains 1, 3 and 4 high; domain 2 low)
overall_rationale: Participant selection excludes reverters on the basis of outcome and drops 34% of eligible participants with undetermined outcome. The outcome is a clinical diagnosis that incorporates the cognitive predictors and is made with knowledge of them. The analysis has few events per predictor, no calibration, undescribed separation of tuning and evaluation, possible preprocessing leakage, an untuned comparator and no external validation. Any high domain gives overall high risk.

applicability.rationale: ADNI research volunteers (mean education 16 years) restricted to those with complete NP and MRI data at five 6-monthly visits and a determinable 48-month status.
The model needs MRI and 15 NP tests at five visits over two years, which is rarely available in routine care.
MCI-to-AD conversion within 2 years by ADNI clinical criteria matches the review's question.
